verdict: Under the editorial surface this codebase has real, verified accessibility engineering: reduce-motion gates on every major animation site (I sampled ~10 — sweeps, shaders, draw-ins, cascades all gate or pause), Dynamic Type by construction via Font.custom(relativeTo:), and honest sentence-length text alternatives on every custom Canvas visual. But the brand's "quiet" register crosses into exclusion exactly where the 35+ / on-medication audience (presbyopia, GLP-1-associated transient vision changes) needs it most: the entire tracked-caps wayfinding tier renders at 2.74:1, the 12-page becoming pager is signposted by ~1.3:1 five-point dots, and the checkable-day contract (long-press mark-as-done, live steps count) never reaches VoiceOver. The must-fix list is short and cheap — mostly one token and a handful of modifiers — which makes shipping it in the v7 redesign a bargain.

keep.what: The reduce-motion gating pattern — verified, not just claimed. JKSilkSweep guards the sweep (JKSilkSweep.swift:35), JKSignalVisuals pauses its TimelineView shaders and short-circuits every draw-in (`paused: reduceMotion || !isLive` line 145; `if reduceMotion { drawn = true; return }` at 226/450/678/816/906/1047/1176), BreathingShadow substitutes a static shadow (Tokens.swift:828-838), ModernEntrance nils the animation (Tokens.swift:925), JKKcalBar.arm() and TodayStateBand's LANDED moment both branch on it.
keep.why: This is the hardest a11y discipline to retrofit and it is already systemic; the v7 redesign should inherit the pattern (gate at the component, offer a static equivalent, never just skip the content).

keep.what: Dynamic Type by construction: Typo.font() routes everything through Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:) with an explicit comment that the old fixed-size UIFont bridge was repaired (Tokens.swift:20-28), and JKMasthead drops the archetype note at accessibility sizes via `typeSize.isAccessibilitySize` (JKMasthead.swift:29,49) — a designed absence, not clipping.
keep.why: Custom-font apps usually ship frozen type; here the serif hero, captions, and numerals all scale, and there is precedent in-code for AX-size layout adaptation to extend.

keep.what: Sentence-length text alternatives on every custom visual: JKWindowHorizon reads "fasting since 8:12pm, about 11 hours so far" (JKSignalVisuals.swift:204-209), weigh-in dots read "5 weigh-ins across the last two weeks" (890), sugar bars read "sugar lands mostly in your evenings" (1024), all via accessibilityElement(children: .ignore); decorative JKMark glyphs and PaperGrainBackground are accessibilityHidden (JKMarks.swift:132, Tokens.swift:808).
keep.why: Data-bearing labels in jeni's own voice mean VoiceOver users get the insight, not a shape description — keep this exact grammar for every new signal visual in v7.

keep.what: Row grammar: each rhythm row and day-rail cell is ONE accessible element with a state-bearing label and action hint — "trend check, first one in a while" + "opens trend check" (JKReadingDay.swift:633-635), "day 11, kept" + "opens the day's receipt" (225-227), future days "day 13, to come" (230).
keep.why: Collapsed elements with hints are the correct model for a list-of-doors Home; the fix needed (custom actions, live values) builds on this foundation rather than replacing it.

keep.what: The tappableArea() token (Tokens.swift:1051-1062) and its use in JKQuietMark, which wraps a 17pt glyph in an invisible 44pt target (JKFoundation.swift:104-106).
keep.why: The 44pt intent is already tokenized and documented — the remaining sub-44 controls are call-site omissions, not a missing system.

problems.title: The entire tracked-caps wayfinding tier fails contrast at 2.74:1
problems.evidence: Palette.cocoaTertiary = #3D2A2A at 48% opacity (Tokens.swift:446) over cream #FDF6F4 computes to 2.74:1 (needs 4.5:1 at 10-11pt; below even the 3:1 large-text bar). Consumers: JKSectionSeam titles "SIGNALS" / "TODAY'S FOOD" / "CLOSING THE DAY" (JKSignalVisuals.swift:1305), masthead date "MONDAY, JULY 27" (JKMasthead.swift:91), "FROM JENI" affordance (JKVoice.swift:47), "IF YOU FEEL LIKE IT" at a further 0.85 opacity = ~2.4:1 (TodayView.swift:490), becoming's "WEEK 2 OF 20 · FINDING STEADY" and "STARTED/NOW/GOAL" stat labels, WindowSheet's "WHY FASTING HELPS" (TodaySignals.swift:488-491), chat's "YOUR COACH · MONDAY" — visible in screenshots 01-08.
problems.detail: This is not decorative text: it is every section boundary, the date, and every stat label — the app's navigation skeleton. WCAG 1.4.3 fail on the primary background for the exact audience (35+, on-medication with documented transient vision changes) the roadmap targets. The dark one-thing card's quiet tier passes (cream at 55-62% on cocoa ≈ 5:1+) — only the cream-background tier is broken, so this is a single-token repair: 0.48 → 0.66 opacity computes to ~4.5:1 while staying visibly quieter than cocoaSecondary.

problems.title: VoiceOver cannot mark a beat done — the long-press override is gesture-only
problems.evidence: JKRhythmRow and JKOneThingCard attach onLongPress via JKTapWithLongPress's simultaneousGesture (JKReadingDay.swift:338-347, 617) and collapse children with accessibilityElement(children: .ignore); repo-wide grep finds accessibilityAction on only 3 files (OV5Ruler, LessonReaderView, HoldToPromiseButton) — none on Today.
problems.detail: The v6.4 founder call made the day "a checkable list," but a VoiceOver or Switch Control user's only exposed action is "opens X" — she must enter and complete the full module to check anything off; MarkAsDoneSheet is unreachable. One `.accessibilityAction(named: "mark as done")` mirroring onLongPress on both components restores parity.

problems.title: Live steps count and progress are invisible to VoiceOver
problems.evidence: JKRhythmRow's label is `"\(title)\(state.isDone ? ", done" : note)"` (JKReadingDay.swift:634) — the liveTrailing "6,420" (screenshot 01, steps row) and JKBeatState.progress are dropped by children: .ignore; JKKcalBar by contrast labels correctly ("860 of about 1,473 calories today", JKGauges.swift:266-267).
problems.detail: A sighted user glances 6,420 of 7,500; a VoiceOver user hears only "7,500 steps, auto-tracked" — an information-parity failure on Home's single auto-tracked number. Append liveTrailing to the label or expose it as accessibilityValue ("6,420 so far").

problems.title: The 12-page story pager is signposted by ~1.3:1, 5pt dots
problems.evidence: JKPageDots: inactive = cocoaTertiary.opacity(0.28) → effective 13% cocoa ≈ 1.27:1 vs the 3:1 non-text minimum, at 5pt diameter (BecomingStoryPages.swift:76-84); it is the ONLY affordance that becoming has 11 more pages (TabView indexDisplayMode: .never, BecomingView.swift:169). Screenshots 04-06: the rail is barely perceptible even in a pristine PNG.
problems.detail: For presbyopic eyes the dots vanish entirely — 12 pages of the app's insight story become undiscoverable, which is a retention problem wearing an accessibility costume. The element has a good "page 1 of 12" label but is not adjustable and not tappable. Raise inactive dots to ≥3:1 and ~8pt, add accessibilityAdjustableAction (and ideally tap-to-jump), or add a small "1 of 12" numeral.

problems.title: Sub-44pt touch targets on high-frequency controls
problems.evidence: Masthead camera JKProminentMark button = 36×36 with no tappableArea (JKMasthead.swift:133) — contrast JKQuietMark which does it right (JKFoundation.swift:106); chat send = 38×38 (JeniChatView.swift:480); evening feeling/plan chips ≈ 34pt tall (9pt vertical padding + 14pt text, TodayStateBand.swift:276-283, 258-264); evening journal save check = 32×32 (TodayStateBand.swift:406); "add sleep · one tap" chip ≈ 31pt (TodaySignals.swift:185-193).
problems.detail: The snap camera is the app's hero action and the send button is chat's only submit — both under HIG's 44pt floor for an audience where fine-motor precision declines with age. The fix is the existing `.tappableArea()` modifier at 5 call sites; day-rail cells already pass (~50pt full-cell contentShape).

problems.title: Accessibility text sizes truncate and collide: negative serif leading is fixed while glyphs scale
problems.evidence: Negative leading is hardcoded in points — JKCoachLine .lineSpacing(-4) at 22pt serif (JKVoice.swift:33), JKOneThingCard .lineSpacing(-2) (JKReadingDay.swift:439), Typo.questionHeroLineGap = -17 / programHeroLineGap = -22 (Tokens.swift:205,165) — while the fonts scale up to ~2.4× at AX5. Rows clamp: JKRhythmRow title .lineLimit(1).minimumScaleFactor(0.8) (JKReadingDay.swift:561-562), one-thing done state lineLimit(1) (417-422), day-rail ribbon lineLimit(1) (188-189).
problems.detail: At AX3+ the serif hero's lines physically overlap (a -4pt gap tuned for 22pt is applied to ~44pt glyphs) and row titles shrink-then-truncate — precisely for the Larger-Text-without-VoiceOver users the 35+ persona produces. Needs one AX-size pass: read dynamicTypeSize, zero the negative leading and lift line limits at .accessibility1+, following the masthead's existing isAccessibilitySize precedent.

problems.title: Rose accent used as small text fails AA (3.53:1)
problems.evidence: Palette.accent #C4677A on cream = 3.53:1; "that plate landed ♥" renders it at 16pt italic serif (TodayStateBand.swift:49-51); becoming's "lb" unit marker and chat accents are smaller still. Palette.jeweledRose #7A2E3F = 8.59:1 already exists (Tokens.swift:412).
problems.detail: 3.53:1 passes only for ≥18.7pt/bold text. The landed line is ephemeral (3.4s) which lowers stakes, but the compliant jeweled-rose sibling is already a token — swap small-size rose text to it, or reserve accent for ≥19pt.

problems.title: Terminal hearts are vocalized: VoiceOver appends "black heart suit" across the app
problems.evidence: \u{2665}\u{FE0E} is embedded in strings that become accessibility labels: JKOneThingCard rest-day title (TodayView.swift:428), plan receipt "3 of 4 done ♥" via combined JKReceiptRow (TodayStateBand.swift:322), "even coffee counts. no grading here ♥" (TodayView.swift:638), masthead "on a break ♥" (690), sleep/medication captions (TodaySignals.swift:168,230,237).
problems.detail: The brand's terminal-punctuation heart becomes a spoken non-word at the end of most sentences — mildly degrading jeni's voice for exactly the users who experience her only through speech. One helper that strips U+2665/U+2661 when composing accessibility labels (visible text untouched) fixes it app-wide.

recommendations.title: Codify a contrast floor as design-system law, and retint the quiet tier to meet it
recommendations.detail: One token change: Palette.cocoaTertiary from opacity(0.48) to opacity(0.66) (~4.5:1 on cream; still clearly quieter than cocoaSecondary's 5.32:1), plus sweep the few call sites that stack further opacity on it (TodayView.swift:490's .opacity(0.85), JKSectionSeam detail's 0.85). Then encode the law the way Signals.swift encodes safety law: a unit test in the existing suite asserting every Palette text token ≥4.5:1 on bgPrimary/bgElevated and every indicator token ≥3:1 — the palette already has precedent (textSecondary and state colors were deepened for AA per Tokens.swift:389-420 comments; the 48% tier was simply missed). This survives any v7 repaint.

recommendations.title: Give the checkable day its VoiceOver contract: custom actions + live values
recommendations.detail: On JKRhythmRow and JKOneThingCard add `.accessibilityAction(named: "mark as done")` wired to the existing onLongPress closure (skip when nil or isProgressRow), and append liveTrailing/progress to the label or set accessibilityValue ("6,420 so far" on steps; the check-ring state is already spoken via ", done"). ~15 lines total, restores full parity with the sighted checkable-list contract from v6.4.

recommendations.title: Make the 12-page story discoverable: legible, adjustable, tappable dots
recommendations.detail: JKPageDots: inactive fill to cocoaSecondary-class (≥3:1), 8pt diameter, wrap in a Button-per-dot or add `.accessibilityAdjustableAction` driving pageIndex, and consider a numeral ("1 of 12") beside the rail at AX sizes. This is dual-purpose: the same change that fixes WCAG non-text contrast also fixes the sighted discoverability cliff hiding 11 of becoming's 12 insight pages — directly serving the north star's "the app notices patterns" promise, which only lands if she can find the pages.

recommendations.title: Apply tappableArea() to the five sub-44pt controls
recommendations.detail: JKProminentMark's 36pt camera (JKMasthead.swift:133), chat send 38pt (JeniChatView.swift:480), evening feeling + tonight-plan chips (TodayStateBand.swift:258-283 — raise vertical padding to 12 or add the modifier), journal save check 32pt (TodayStateBand.swift:406), "add sleep" chip (TodaySignals.swift:185). The modifier already exists and JKQuietMark shows the pattern; this is a one-hour sweep.

recommendations.title: Ship an AX-size layout pass for the serif register
recommendations.detail: Read @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize) in JKCoachLine, JKOneThingCard, JKRhythmRow, and the hero-token call sites: at .accessibility1+ set lineSpacing to 0 (instead of the fixed -4/-2/-17/-22 negative leading), lift lineLimit(1) to 2 with truncation off for row titles, and let notes wrap below the title. Follow JKMasthead's existing isAccessibilitySize precedent (drop ornament, keep data). Verify with the existing screenshot-walker UI tests run at AX3 — the harness already exists (OnboardingV5WalkerUITests pattern).

recommendations.title: Strip decorative hearts from spoken labels with one helper
recommendations.detail: Add `String.a11yStripped` (removes U+2665/U+2661 + trailing whitespace) and apply where labels are composed: JKOneThingCard.a11yLabel, JKRhythmRow label, JKReceiptRow (switch to explicit label instead of children:.combine where hearts appear), masthead note, caption texts under signals. Visible brand voice unchanged; spoken voice stops saying "black heart suit" every third sentence.

recommendations.title: Move small rose text to jeweledRose
recommendations.detail: "that plate landed ♥" (TodayStateBand.swift:51), becoming's small "lb"/unit markers, and any sub-19pt Palette.accent text → Palette.jeweledRose (8.59:1, same rose family, already reserved for editorial moments per its token comment). Keep #C4677A for large numerals, fills, and the live ember dot where 3:1 non-text passes.

one_transformative_move: Make "quiet" mean calm, not faint — encode accessibility floors as tested design-system law: retint cocoaTertiary to ~66% (4.5:1), raise pager/indicator tokens to 3:1, and add a Tokens contrast unit test to the existing 242-test suite so no future "luxury restraint" pass can ship below the floor. It is the one change that makes the whole app readable for the 35+ on-medication women the product is converging on, it costs one token plus a test file, and every other finding (dots, captions, stat labels, date eyebrow) collapses into it — a companion who is "already paying attention" must first be effortlessly seen.
